***
A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.

```lean
Set.Nonempty.{u} {α : Type u} (s : Set α) : Prop
```
***
The property `s.Nonempty` expresses the fact that the set `s` is not empty. It should be used
in theorem assumptions instead of `∃ x, x ∈ s` or `s ≠ ∅` as it gives access to a nice API thanks
to the dot notation.

***
A subset of α is directed if there is an element of the set `≼`-above any
pair of elements in the set.

```lean
UniformConvergenceCLM.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜₁ : Type u_1} {𝕜₂ : Type u_2} [NormedField 𝕜₁] [NormedField 𝕜₂]
  (σ : 𝕜₁ →+* 𝕜₂) {E : Type u_3} (F : Type u_4) [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜₁ E] [TopologicalSpace E] [AddCommGroup F]
  [Module 𝕜₂ F] [TopologicalSpace F] [TopologicalAddGroup F] : Set (Set E) → Type (max u_3 u_4)
```
***
Given `E` and `F` two topological vector spaces and `𝔖 : Set (Set E)`, then
`UniformConvergenceCLM σ F 𝔖` is a type synonym of `E →SL[σ] F` equipped with the "topology of
uniform convergence on the elements of `𝔖`".

If the continuous linear image of any element of `𝔖` is bounded, this makes `E →SL[σ] F` a
topological vector space.
